title: 31-Year-Old Swimmer Breaks Record at Asian Games!
summary:
Can you still be a champion at 31? Xu Jiayu just proved you can! At the 2026 Asian Games in Tokyo, the Chinese swimmer won the men's 100m backstroke in 51.98 seconds. That's a new Games Record!

Xu is 31 years old, which is pretty old for a swimmer. But he's been winning Chinese national titles for 13 years straight, starting when he was just 18. He's also won five Olympic medals. Not bad, right?

The first day of the Asian Games was full of fast swimming. In the women's 200m butterfly, Yu Zidi from China won with a time of 2:05.08. She's the youngest swimmer ever to medal at the World Championships!

In the women's 50m breaststroke, Tang Qianting touched the wall in 29.45 seconds. That's super fast — under 30 seconds! The silver medal went to Satomi Suzuki from Japan. She's 35 years old and swam 29.91 seconds, her first time under 30 seconds. She also set a new Japanese record.

Finally, China's women's 4x100m freestyle relay team — Yu Yiting, Zhang Yufei, Cheng Yujie, and Wu Qingfeng — won gold in 3:33.10, another Games Record. Zhang Yufei swam her leg in 52.99 seconds, and Wu Qingfeng anchored with 52.93. What a start to the week!
why_it_matters: It shows that people can keep getting better as they get older, so it's worth sticking with a sport or a skill even when you're not the youngest one there.

background_read: The Asian Games are a huge sports competition for countries across Asia, held every four years — a bit like the Olympics, but for one continent.
Tokyo (the capital city of Japan) has hosted many big international sports events, including the Olympics.
Most swimmers swim their fastest in their teens or early twenties and many stop racing before 30, so winning at 31 is unusual.
Zhang Yufei (a Chinese swimmer who has won Olympic gold) was one of the swimmers on China's record-breaking relay team.

WHAT: Xu won the men's 100m backstroke in 51.98 seconds, setting a new Games Record on day one
WHERE: The 2026 Asian Games in Tokyo, Japan
WHY: At 31 Xu is old for a swimmer, but 13 years of national titles and five Olympic medals show experience can beat youth

perspectives.description: Age is just a number — his years of training and experience helped him beat much younger swimmers and set a new Games Record.
Yu Zidi, the youngest swimmer ever to medal at the World Championships, shows that young athletes are rising fast and pushing the sport forward.
Satomi Suzuki, at 35, swam under 30 seconds for the first time and set a Japanese record, proving veteran swimmers can still improve.
